akhfash:3-3.t: He said ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is: "your hatefulness is great as hatefulness" (كَبُرَ مَقْتُكُم مَقْتاً); then He said ﴿أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا لاَ تَفْعَلُونَ﴾, that is: your saying (قولُكم).

akhfash:13-13.t: [And] He said ﴿وَأُخْرَىٰ تُحِبُّونَهَا﴾: He means "and another trade" (وتجارةٌ أُخْرَى).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾, i.e. declared Him transcendent; so the lām is added (mazīda), and مَا is used rather than مَنْ, giving predominance (taghlīb) to the majority. ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَ تَقُولُونَ﴾ in asking for jihad ﴿مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾, since you were routed at Uḥud?

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿كَبُرَ﴾ it is grave ﴿مَقْتًا﴾: tamyīz (specification); ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ تَقُولُوا﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of كَبُرَ; ﴿مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ﴾ helps and honours ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. ranged in rows, ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيَانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ﴾ joined one part to another, firm.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَ﴾ mention ﴿إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ لِمَ تُؤْذُونَنِي﴾ — they said he was آدَرُ, i.e. with a swollen testicle, and he was not so; and they called him a liar — ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ for affirmation ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ أَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and a messenger is to be respected. ﴿فَلَمَّا زَاغُوا﴾ turned aside from the truth by harming him, ﴿أَزَاغَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ He inclined them away from guidance, in accordance with what He had decreed in pre-eternity; ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾ the disbelievers in His knowledge.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَ﴾ mention ﴿إِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ — he did not say "O my people" because he had no kinship among them — ﴿إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ﴾ before me ﴿مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَمُبَشِّرًا بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ﴾. The Exalted said: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ﴾ — Aḥmad came to the disbelievers — ﴿بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ the signs and marks, ﴿قَالُوا هَذَا﴾, i.e. what was brought, ﴿سِحْرٌ﴾ — and in a reading [سَاحِرٌ], i.e. the one who brought it — ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ clear.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾, i.e. no one, ﴿أَظْلَمُ﴾ is more severe in wrongdoing ﴿مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾ by attributing a partner and a son to Him and describing His signs as sorcery, ﴿وَهُوَ يُدْعَى إِلَى الْإِسْلَامِ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِئُوا﴾: accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أَنْ, and the lām is added; ﴿نُورَ اللَّهِ﴾ His law and His proofs ﴿بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ by their sayings that it is sorcery, poetry and soothsaying; ﴿وَاللَّهُ مُتِمٌّ﴾ making manifest ﴿نُورَهُ﴾ — and in a reading [مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ], as a genitive construct (iḍāfa) — ﴿وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ﴾ to raise it high ﴿عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ over all the opposing religions, ﴿وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى تِجَارَةٍ تُنْجِيكُمْ﴾, without tashdīd and with it, ﴿مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ painful? It is as though they said "Yes", so He said:

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ you continue in faith ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is better for you; so do it.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿يَغْفِرْ﴾: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you do it, He will forgive" ﴿لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ وَمَسَاكِنَ طَيِّبَةً فِي جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ of abiding; ﴿ذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَ﴾ He will give you a blessing ﴿أُخْرَى تُحِبُّونَهَا نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ of victory and conquest.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا أَنْصَارًا لِلَّهِ﴾ for His religion — and in a reading [أَنْصَارَ اللَّهِ], as a genitive construct (iḍāfa) — ﴿كَمَا قَالَ﴾ etc.: the meaning is "as the disciples were so", which قَالَ indicates; ﴿عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ لِلْحَوَارِيِّينَ مَنْ أَنْصَارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. who are the helpers who will be with me, heading towards the help of Allah? ﴿قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنْصَارُ اللَّهِ﴾. The disciples (al-ḥawāriyyūn) were the chosen ones of Jesus and the first to believe in him; they were twelve men, (the name being) from al-ḥawr, which is pure whiteness; and it is said they were fullers who would whiten (yuḥawwirūn) clothes, i.e. bleach them. ﴿فَآمَنَتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ in Jesus and said that he is the servant of Allah, raised to heaven, ﴿وَكَفَرَتْ طَائِفَةٌ﴾ for their saying that he is the son of Allah, Who raised him to Himself; and the two groups fought each other. ﴿فَأَيَّدْنَا﴾ We strengthened ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ of the two groups ﴿عَلَى عَدُوِّهِمْ﴾ the disbelieving group, ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا ظَاهِرِينَ﴾ victorious.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿سَبَّحَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted [word that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; and ﴿ما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ما في السموات». ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and two khabars (predicates), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ «أيّ» is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for «أيها»; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿لِمَ﴾ «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what comes after them; ﴿تَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ negating [particle] and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿كَبُرَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿مَقْتاً﴾ tamyīz (specification); ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ an adverb of place, annexed to the Name of Majesty; ﴿أَنْ تَقُولُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «كبر..» is its fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ negating [particle] and an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿يُحِبُّ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿يُقاتِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فِي سَبِيلِهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿صَفًّا﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيانٌ﴾ «كأنّ», its noun and its khabar; ﴿مَرْصُوصٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قالَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, «إذ» is an adverb of time, and a past verb; ﴿مُوسى﴾ its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿يا قَوْمِ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), in the accusative (manṣūb) with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, which has been dropped for lightness; ﴿لِمَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what comes after them, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿تُؤْذُونَنِي﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil, the nūn being for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿قَدْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) and an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿أَنِّي﴾ «أنّ» and its noun; ﴿رَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾ its khabar (predicate), annexed to the Name of Majesty; ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to «رسول», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أنّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «تعلمون». And the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لما﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya); ﴿زاغُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of a genitive by iḍāfa; ﴿أَزاغَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, the Name of Majesty being its fāʿil; ﴿قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi; and the clause «فلما..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject) «[Translator's note: the quoted word is printed with a kasra in the source; in the verse it is «وَاللَّهُ», nominative.]»; ﴿لا يَهْدِي﴾ negating [particle] and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْقَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْفاسِقِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قالَ عِيسَى﴾ the i'rab of its like has been given before; ﴿ابْنُ﴾ a badal (substitute) for «عيسى», and ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to «إسرائيل», in the accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ, and the vocative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾ «إنّ», its noun and its khabar (predicate), which is annexed to the Name of Majesty; ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رسول», and the nominal clause is the object of the saying; ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿لِما﴾ both are attached to «مصدقا»; ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place annexed to ﴿يَدَيَّ﴾; ﴿مِنَ التَّوْراةِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وَمُبَشِّراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «مصدقا»; ﴿بِرَسُولٍ﴾ both are attached to «مبشرا»; ﴿يَأْتِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول»; ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِي﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar, and the clause is a second naʿt of «رسول». ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لِما﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya) «[Translator's note: the source prints «لِما» here; the word in the verse is «لَمّا».]»; ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by iḍāfa; ﴿بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿هذا سِحْرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ a naʿt, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying, and the clause «قالوا..» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «لما», with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿مَنْ أَظْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مِمَّنِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أظلم»; ﴿افْتَرى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْكَذِبَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿يُدْعى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent; ﴿إِلَى الْإِسْلامِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «هو», and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the i'rab of its like has been given before.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لِيُطْفِؤُا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit «أن» after the lām of purpose (lām al-taʿlīl), the wāw being its fāʿil; ﴿نُورَ اللَّهِ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to the Name of Majesty; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿بِأَفْواهِهِمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿اللَّهُ مُتِمُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿نُورِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لَوْ كَرِهَ الْكافِرُونَ﴾ «لو» is concessive-connective (waṣliyya), and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَرْسَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿رَسُولَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; ﴿بِالْهُدى﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿وَدِينِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الهدى»; ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit «أن» after the lām of purpose, the hāʾ being its mafʿūl bihi and the fāʿil latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to «أرسل»; ﴿عَلَى الدِّينِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿كُلِّهِ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿لَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ﴾ «لو» is concessive-connective (waṣliyya), and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has been given before, and ﴿هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ﴾ «هل» is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿عَلى تِجارَةٍ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿تُنْجِيكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «تجارة»; ﴿مِنْ عَذابٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ a naʿt of «عذاب».

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَتُجاهِدُونَ﴾ conjoined to «تؤمنون»; ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿بِأَمْوالِكُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb as well; ﴿وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ conjoined to «أموالكم»; ﴿ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to «خير»; ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ «إن» is conditional and makes the verb jussive, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the tāʾ being its noun; ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «كنتم», and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿يَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it falls as the answer to the command understood from His saying «تؤمنون بالله», the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ذُنُوبَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause has no grammatical position; ﴿وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يغفر لكم»; ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and an imperfect verb «[Translator's note: «and an imperfect verb» evidently refers to «تَجْرِي», which is not quoted in the source.]»; ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات»; ﴿وَمَساكِنَ﴾ conjoined to «جنات»; ﴿طَيِّبَةً﴾ a naʿt of «مساكن»; ﴿فِي جَنَّاتِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿عَدْنٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ a naʿt, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَأُخْرى﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), the fronted khabar (predicate) being omitted; ﴿تُحِبُّونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «أخرى»; ﴿نَصْرٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position; ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نصر»; ﴿وَفَتْحٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «نصر»; ﴿قَرِيبٌ﴾ a naʿt of «فتح»; ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has been given before. ﴿كُونُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, the wāw being its noun; ﴿أَنْصارَ اللَّهِ﴾ its khabar (predicate), annexed to the Name of Majesty, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿كَما﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿قالَ عِيسَى﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿ابْنُ﴾ a badal (substitute) for «عيسى»; ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿لِلْحَوارِيِّينَ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «ما» and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the kāf; ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَنْصارِي﴾ khabar; ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿قالَ الْحَوارِيُّونَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿نَحْنُ أَنْصارُ اللَّهِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿فَآمَنَتْ طائِفَةٌ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنْ بَنِي﴾ both are attached to an omitted naʿt of «طائفة»; ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause ﴿وَكَفَرَتْ طائِفَةٌ﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَيَّدْنَا الَّذِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil, the relative noun being its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلى عَدُوِّهِمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا ظاهِرِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أصبح», its noun and its khabar, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا أَنْصارَ اللَّهِ) كونوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, the wāw is its noun (ism), and أنصار الله is its khabar (predicate); the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) to أنصار. It has also been read أنصارا لله, in which case لله would be a naʿt (adjective) of أنصارا. (كَما قالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ لِلْحَوارِيِّينَ مَنْ أَنْصارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ) The grammarians have disagreed greatly about this kāf, and the upshot of what they have mentioned is that it admits three possibilities:
1- It is in the position of accusative on the implication of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "We said that to them, just as ʿĪsā said."
2- It is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); it has been said that this is questionable, since they are not being commanded to "be a being".
3- It is speech construed according to its meaning rather than its wording, and this is the view al-Zamakhsharī inclined to, for he said: «If you ask: what makes the comparison sound, when its apparent sense is a comparison of their being helpers with ʿĪsā's saying "Who are my helpers unto Allah?" I answer: the comparison is construed according to the meaning, and on that basis it is sound; what is meant is: be helpers of Allah just as the disciples were helpers of ʿĪsā when he said to them, "Who are my helpers unto Allah?"».
The meaning of أنصاري إلى الله, and the transitivity of this word with إلى, has already been discussed in Āl ʿImrān. من is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and أنصاري is the khabar; إلى الله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "heading towards the support of Allah". What follows is the text of al-Zamakhsharī's words: «If you ask: what is the meaning of His saying من أنصاري إلى الله? I answer: its meaning must correspond to the disciples' reply when they said "We are the helpers of Allah", and what corresponds to it is that the meaning be: who are my troops heading towards the support of Allah? The annexation in أنصاري is different from the annexation in أنصار الله, for the meaning of "We are the helpers of Allah" is "We are those who support Allah", whereas the meaning of من أنصاري is "Who, among the helpers, are those who are particular to me and will be with me in supporting Allah?" It is not sound for its meaning to be "Who will support me along with Allah?", because that does not correspond to the reply; and the proof of this is the reading of those who read: من أنصار الله».
(قالَ الْحَوارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنْصارُ اللَّهِ) قال الحواريون is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the الحواريون are his chosen ones, and they were the first to believe; the discussion of this word has been given in detail earlier. نحن is a mubtadaʾ and أنصار الله a khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). It is a case of annexing a descriptive (waṣf) to its object, i.e. "We are those who support Allah", that is, His religion [Translator's note: the source prints «دنيه», evidently a misprint for «دينه» "His religion"; translated accordingly].
(فَآمَنَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ وَكَفَرَتْ طائِفَةٌ) The fāʾ conjoins to omitted clauses which must be supplied, i.e. "When ʿĪsā was raised to heaven, people split into two factions concerning him, so a faction believed"; طائفة is the fāʿil of آمنت, and من بني إسرائيل is a naʿt of طائفة; وكفرت طائفة is conjoined to فآمنت طائفة.
(فَأَيَّدْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلى عَدُوِّهِمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا ظاهِرِينَ) The fāʾ likewise conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "so the two factions fought one another". أيدنا is a verb and its fāʿil, الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); على عدوهم is attached to أيدنا. فأصبحوا is conjoined to فأيدنا; the wāw is its noun and ظاهرين its khabar, i.e. "prevailing, overpowering".

dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَقْتاً): [Al-Zamakhsharī] said in al-Asās: «مقته مقتا: it is hatred arising from an ugly matter; and in this connection a man's marrying his stepmother [Translator's note: the source has "رابّته", strictly "his stepdaughter"; the usual expression refers to marrying the father's wife] was called نكاح المقت (the marriage of loathing): «إنه كان فاحشة ومقتا». And مقت إلى الناس مقاتة, like بغض بغاضة (he became hateful to people); he is ممقوت and مقيت.»
(مَرْصُوصٌ): stuck together, one part upon another, as if built with lead (al-raṣāṣ). It has been said: المرصوص is that whose parts are joined together and level; it has also been said: bound with lead; and it has been said: the compacted, from تراصّ الأسنان (the teeth being set close). In al-Miṣbāḥ: «الرصّ is the joining of parts of a building to one another and its firmness; its pattern is that of ردّ.» Among the remarkable features of rāʾ and ṣād, when they occur as the first and second radicals of a word, is that they indicate the meaning of compactness and firmness, and of readiness for a matter. You say رصدته, ارتصدته and ترصدته: I sat for him on his way, watching for him; and تراصد الرجلان (the two men watched for each other). Dhū al-Rumma said:
يراصدها في جوف حدباء ضيق ... على المرء إلا ما تخرّق حالها
(He lies in wait for them inside a narrow, humped [hide], tight upon a man except where its state has been torn.)
And سبع رصيد: a beast of prey that lies in wait to spring. "I am lying in wait for you (أنا لك بالمرصد والمرصاد)", i.e. you will not escape me. "I have prepared (أرصدت) this army for fighting, this horse for the chase, and this money for paying dues", when you have made it ready for that and put it in its way. رصع التاج: he adorned the crown with stars of ornament; رصّع الطائر عشه بالقضبان والريش: the bird brought the twigs and feathers of its nest close together and wove it; أسنانه مرتصعة مرتصّة: his teeth are set close; تراصع العصفوران: the two sparrows mated; and راصع الطائر أنثاه: the bird mated with its female. رصف الحجارة ورصّفها: he set the stones close together; the water ran over الرّصف and الرّصاف, which is laid rock; تراصفوا في الصلاة والقتال: they stood in close ranks in prayer and in fighting; and you say: تراصفوا ثم تقاصفوا (they closed ranks, then crowded upon one another); رصف إحدى قدميه إلى الأخرى: he put one of his feet close to the other; تراصفت أسنانه تراصفا, which is their being set in rows. And figuratively: امرأة رصوف, a woman narrow in the private part; and رجل رصيف, a man firm in his work; and it is said: he gave an answer that was مترّص [Translator's note: so in the source, presumably مُتْرَص, "firmly made"], حصيف (sound), بين (clear), رصيف (firm) — neither feeble nor light. رصن البناء وغيره رصانة: it was firm, so it is رصين; and figuratively: he has a رصين (sound) opinion, and كلام متين رصين (solid, firm speech).

* I'rab:
(سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): the i'rab of this verse has preceded at the opening of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, so renew your acquaintance with it.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَ تَقُولُونَ ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ): لم: the lām is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun conveying disapproval and rebuke. It has preceded that when a preposition enters upon interrogative ما its alif is dropped, as in بم, فيم, مم, إلام, علام, عمّ and حتام; the alif was dropped only because ما and the preposition resemble a single thing. Its use with the alif dropped has occurred frequently in the speech of the questioner, and the original form has come in use rarely. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تقولون; تقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لا is negating; and the clause تفعلون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.
(كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ تَقُولُوا ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ): كبر is a past verb, i.e. it is grave; مقتا is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil; عند الله: the adverb is attached to an omitted adjective of مقتا, or [to an omitted] ḥāl (circumstantial); and أن تقولوا is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of كبر. The original is "the loathing of their saying became grave", i.e. the loathing consequent upon their saying what they do not do. It is also permissible that كبر be of the category of نعم and بئس, so the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun explained by the indefinite tamyīz, and أن تقولوا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause before it, since it is the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm). The discussion of all that has preceded, and further discussion of this construction will come in the section on rhetoric.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ): إنّ and its noun, and the clause يحب is its predicate; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause يقاتلون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; it is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; في سبيله is attached to يقاتلون; صفا is a ḥāl from the wāw in يقاتلون; كأنّ and its noun, and بنيان is its predicate; مرصوص is a naʿt (adjective) of بنيان; and the clause is a second ḥāl, from the pronoun in صفا, because it means "ranging themselves", so it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila).

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون» there is intensification and repetition, and for this reason this clause has been considered among the most eloquent of speech and the most effective in its meaning, for several reasons:
1- He intended wonder without the form of wonder (taʿajjub), to magnify the matter in the hearts of the hearers, because wonder is only at something that breaks with custom and with its like.
2- He attributed [the verb] to أن تقولوا and put مقتا in the accusative as its explanation, to indicate that their saying what they do not do is pure loathing with no admixture in it.
3- The choice of the word المقت, because it is the most intense and extreme hatred, so much so that the expression "the marriage of loathing" was used, as preceded in the section on vocabulary.
4- Then He was not content to make the hatred great, but made it the most intense and the most outrageous; and His saying عند الله is more effective than that, because if the greatness of its loathing in the sight of Allah is established, its greatness and intensity are complete, and doubts about it are dispelled.
5- The repetition of His saying ما لا تفعلون, which is one expression in one statement. Among the benefits of repetition are inspiring awe and magnifying; otherwise the speech would have been complete if it had been said "كبر مقتا عند الله ذلك", so its repetition is only for the sake of this benefit.
2- The inclusion of the specific under the general. The general prohibition of speech not supported by action has come, and what is intended is the inclusion of the specific matter that came after it, which is His saying: «إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفّا كأنهم بنيان مرصوص». In His mentioning that immediately after the general prohibition there is evidence that the loathing attached to the saying of those who promised steadfastness in fighting the disbelievers and did not fulfil it — just as you say to one who has committed a particular offence: "Do not do what brings shame upon you, and do not revile Zayd." The benefit of such a construction is prohibiting the one thing twice, once included in the general and once singled out specifically; and this is better than prohibiting it specifically twice, for that is counted among the good kinds of repetition [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense seems to require "among the kinds of repetition", i.e. the specific-twice option is mere repetition], whereas this is not repeated, besides the magnification and awe that the generalisation carries.

dervis-irab:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ يا قَوْمِ لِمَ تُؤْذُونَنِي وَقَدْ تَعْلَمُونَ أَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ): a resumptive statement brought to console His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and to settle him upon patience. إذ is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember); the clause قال is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; موسى is the fāʿil (agent); لقومه is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قال. لم: the lām is a preposition and ما an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive by the lām; the secret of dropping the alif of interrogative ما when a preposition precedes it has preceded. تؤذونني is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The wāw is circumstantial; قد is a particle of realisation, even though it has entered upon the imperfect — the imperfect was used only to indicate the continuation of the state. تعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; أني رسول الله is أنّ with its noun and its predicate, and أنّ with what lies in its scope fills the place of the two objects of تعلمون; إليكم is attached to رسول; and the clause وقد تعلمون etc. is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning is that whoever honours Allah honours His Messenger.
(فَلَمَّا زاغُوا أَزاغَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ): the fāʿ is conjunctive; لما is linking or temporal (ḥīniyya); زاغوا is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause أزاغ الله قلوبهم has no grammatical position; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause لا يهدي القوم الظالمين [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has الفاسقين] is the khabar (predicate).
(وَإِذْ قالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ): the adverb is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر"; the clause قال is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; عيسى is the fāʿil; ابن مريم is a badal (substitute) of عيسى; يا بني إسرائيل is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf. He did not say "O my people" because he had no tie of lineage to them, since he had no father, and lineage is only from the father's side, even though his mother Maryam was among the noblest of them in lineage. إنّ and its noun, and رسول الله إليكم is its predicate, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ وَمُبَشِّراً بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ): مصدّقا:
a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in رسول الله, since it is interpreted as مرسل (sent). لما is attached to مصدقا; the adverb is attached to an omitted [word] with no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; يدي is annexed to بين, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is dual; مبشّرا is conjoined to مصدّقا, so it is a ḥāl like it; برسول is attached to مبشّرا; the clause يأتي is an adjective of رسول; من بعدي is attached to يأتي; اسمه is a mubtadaʾ and أحمد its khabar, and the clause is a second adjective.
(فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ): the fāʿ is resumptive; لما is linking or temporal; جاءهم is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; بالبيّنات is attached to جاءهم; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position; and the clause هذا سحر مبين, made of the mubtadaʾ and khabar, is in the position of the accusative as the object of their saying.

* Benefits:
The scholars of Arabic say that قد accompanies the past to bring it close to the present; from this is the muezzin's saying قد قامت الصلاة (the prayer has [just] been established). Its accompanying the past also contains the meaning of expectation; that is why Sībawayh said: قد فعل is the answer to لمّا يفعل (he has not yet done); and al-Khalīl said: this statement is for people who are waiting for it. As for [its use] with the imperfect, it conveys paucity, like ربما, as in their saying: إن الكذوب قد يصدق (the liar sometimes tells the truth). So since its meaning with the imperfect is paucity, and in the verse it has entered upon an imperfect, the right explanation is that this is of the kind of speech by which they intend excess in the opposite of what [the form] expresses; قد in this sense is the counterpart of ربما in His saying «ربما يودّ الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين», for there it is more effective than كم in expressing abundance. Just as ربما was used for abundance, contrary to its original meaning of paucity, so is the use of قد here, to express the abundance of their knowledge, i.e. the realisation of its emphasis, contrary to its original meaning of paucity.

dervis-irab:7-13.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُوَ يُدْعى إِلَى الْإِسْلامِ): the wāw is resumptive; من is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, i.e. "no one", in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); أظلم is the khabar (predicate); ممّن is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أظلم; the clause افترى is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; على الله is attached to افترى; and الكذب is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). وهو: the wāw is circumstantial; هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يدعى is the khabar of هو, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); i.e. his Lord calls him, on the tongue of His Prophet, to Islam, in which lies the happiness of both abodes, and in place of answering it he fabricates lies against Allah. يدعى is an imperfect verb in the passive, and إلى الله [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has إلى الإسلام] is attached to يدعى.
(وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يهدي is the khabar; القوم is the mafʿūl bihi and الظالمين is a naʿt (adjective) of القوم.
(يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِؤُا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ): يريدون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ليطفئوا: the parsers have mentioned several views on this lām, the strongest being three:
1- That it is added to the object of the will. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Its original is يريدون أن يطفئوا, as came in Sūrat Barāʾa. It is as if this lām was added with the verb of willing as an emphasis of it, because of the meaning of will it carries in your saying جئتك لإكرامك (I came to you to honour you), just as the lām was added in لا أبا لك as an emphasis of the meaning of annexation in لا أباك.» Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, supporting this view: «The lām in ليطفئوا is an emphasising lām that has entered upon the object, because the implied form is يريدون أن يطفئوا.»
2- That it is the lām of causation and the object is omitted, i.e. they want the nullification of the Qur'an, or the removal of Islam, or the destruction of the Messenger, in order to extinguish.
3- That it is in the sense of accusative أن, and that it puts the verb in the accusative by itself. Al-Farrāʾ said: The Arabs put the lām of kay in place of أن after أراد and أمر; and al-Kisāʾī also held this.
The wording of Abū Ḥayyān, after citing the aforementioned sayings of al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya — he said: «What Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned, that this lām mostly attaches to the object when it is fronted, is not the most frequent; rather, زيدا ضربت is more frequent than لزيد ضربت. As for their saying that the lām is for emphasis and that the implied form is أن يطفئوا, so that the extinguishing is the object of يريدون, it is not the school of Sībawayh and the majority.»
(وَاللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكافِرُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; الله is a mubtadaʾ, متمّ the khabar, and نوره the muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يريدون or of يطفئوا. The wāw is also circumstantial; لو is conditional; كره الكافرون is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl from the preceding ḥāl clause, so it is overlapping (mutadākhila); the answer of لو is omitted, its implied form being "He completes it and makes it prevail".
(هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ): هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar; the clause أرسل is the ṣila; رسوله is the mafʿūl bihi; بالهدى is attached to أرسل or to an omitted ḥāl; دين الحق is conjoined to الهدى; the lām is for causation; يظهره is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its noun are attached to أرسل; على الدين is attached to يظهره; كله is a tawkīd (emphasis); the clause ولو كره المشركون is a ḥāl; the object of كره is omitted, i.e. its being made to prevail; and the answer of لو is also omitted, its implied form being "He makes it prevail".
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى تِجارَةٍ تُنْجِيكُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ): هل is an interrogative particle whose meaning is informing and affirmation, i.e. "I will guide you"; He put it in the form of a question only to arouse eagerness and kindle desire. أدلكم is an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil being latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنا", and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; على تجارة is attached to أدلكم; the clause تنجيكم is an adjective of تجارة; من عذاب is attached to تنجيكم; and أليم is an adjective of عذاب. The account of its revelation, which is impossible [Translator's note: so in the source, "الممتنع"; presumably a misprint for "الممتع", "enjoyable"], will come in the section on benefits.
(تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ): the clause is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is: you believe", or resumptive, in answer to an implied question, as if it were asked: What is the trade? تؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative, but in the sense of a command; this is indicated by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: آمنوا بالله ورسوله وجاهدوا. The benefit of shifting from the command to the statement is to signal the obligation of compliance, as if they had complied, so He informs of a faith and a jihad that exist. بالله is attached to تؤمنون; رسوله is conjoined to بالله; تجاهدون is conjoined to تؤمنون; في سبيل الله is attached to تجاهدون or to an omitted ḥāl; بأموالكم is attached to تجاهدون; and أنفسكم is conjoined to أموالكم.
(ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ): ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ and خير the khabar; لكم is attached to خير; إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause تعلمون is the predicate of كنتم; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then do it"; and the object of تعلمون is omitted for brevity, since it is known, i.e. that it is better for you.
(يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ): يغفر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request understood from His saying تؤمنون, as preceded. It has also been said that it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you do it, He will forgive". The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «يغفر لكم: there are two views on its jussive. One: it is the apodosis of an omitted condition indicated by the speech, its implied form being "if you believe, He will forgive you", تؤمنون being in the sense of آمنوا. The second: it is the answer to what the question indicates, the meaning being "will you accept, if I guide you?" Al-Farrāʾ said it is the answer to the question according to the wording; but this is far-fetched, because His guiding them does not necessitate forgiveness.» The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «If you say: does al-Farrāʾ's saying that it is the answer to هل أدلكم have any justification? I say: its justification is that the object of the guiding is the trade, and the trade is explained as faith and jihad; so it is as if it were said: Will you trade in faith and jihad? He will forgive you.» Ibn al-Munayyir commented on it, saying: «He only justified al-Farrāʾ's parsing in the way he mentioned because, if he had made it the answer to His saying هل أدلكم — "for if I guide you to such-and-such, I will forgive you" — the forgiveness would then follow from the mere fact of His guiding them to good; and it is not so: forgiveness follows only from their doing what He guided them to, not from the guiding itself. So هل أدلكم على تجارة was not interpreted [Translator's note: reading "أوّل" as "أُوِّل"] as "will you trade in faith and jihad" except so that forgiveness would follow from the doing of faith and jihad, not from the guiding. But this interpretation is not needed, for when the gist of the speech comes to "Shall I guide you? I will forgive you", it joins the likes of the saying of Allah the Exalted: «قل لعبادي الذين آمنوا يقيموا الصلاة», for He made the performing of prayer follow from the command to it, as if He said: for if you say to them "establish [prayer]", they will establish it.»
(وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): يدخلكم is conjoined to يغفر, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري is an adjective of جنات; من تحتها is attached to تجري; and الأنهار is the fāʿil.
(وَمَساكِنَ طَيِّبَةً فِي جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ): مساكن is conjoined to جنات; طيبة is an adjective of مساكن; and في جنات عدن is a second adjective.
(ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the forgiveness and admission into the gardens; الفوز is the khabar and العظيم an adjective of الفوز.
(وَأُخْرى تُحِبُّونَها نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw
is a conjunction; أخرى is a postponed mubtadaʾ and its fronted khabar is omitted, i.e. "you have another blessing or reward". It may also be accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and He grants you another", the clause تحبونها being an adjective of أخرى; or accusative by an implied verb explained by تحبونها, so that it is of the category of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the governor), and in that case the clause تحبونها is not an adjective, because it explains the governor before أخرى. نصر is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "that other blessing is help from Allah", or a badal (substitute) of أخرى if you parse it as a mubtadaʾ; من الله is an adjective of نصر; فتح is conjoined to نصر; and قريب is an adjective. وبشّر: the wāw is conjunctive and بشّر is an imperative verb, conjoined to تؤمنون because it has the sense of a command, as preceded.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله» there is an allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), representing their state in striving to nullify the truth by the state of one who blows at the light of the sun with his mouth to extinguish it, in mockery and derision of them. It has also been said that the metaphor is explicit (taṣrīḥiyya), and the extinguishing is a tarshīḥ (consolidation of the metaphor).

* Benefits:
Muqātil said: This verse — «يا أيها الذين آمنوا هل أدلكم على تجارة تنجيكم من عذاب أليم» up to His saying «وبشّر المؤمنين» — was revealed concerning ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn. That was because he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If you would permit me, I would divorce Khawla, become a monk, castrate myself, forbid myself meat, never sleep at night and never break my fast by day." He ﷺ said: "Marriage is part of my sunna, and there is no monasticism in Islam; the monasticism of my community is only jihad in the way of Allah, and the castration of my community is fasting. Do not forbid the good things Allah has made lawful for you. Part of my sunna is that I sleep and stand [in prayer], break my fast and fast; whoever turns away from my sunna is not of me." ʿUthmān said: "I wish, O Prophet of Allah, that I knew which trade is most beloved to Allah, so that I might trade in it." Then [the verse] was revealed.

farraa:10-11.t:
His saying: ﴿هَلْ أَدُلُّكمْ عَلَىٰ تِجَارَةٍ تُنجِيكُم مِّنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: آمنوا. Had it been said in our reading: أن تؤمنوا [it would have been valid], because it is an explanation (tarjama) of the trade. When you explain a preceding noun by a verb, it is permissible both to include أن and to omit it: you say to a man: هل لك فى خير تقوم بنا إلى المسجد فنصلى (would you like something good: you go with us to the mosque and we pray), and if you said: أن تقوم إلى المسجد it would be correct. Similar to this — where something explains what precedes it in two ways — is His saying: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإِنسَانُ إِلَى طَعَامِهِ﴾: أَنَّا and إِنَّا. Whoever says أَنَّا here is like the one who puts (أَنْ) before يقوم, and whoever says إِنَّا is like the one who drops (أنْ) from تقوم. Similar to it is: ﴿عَاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا﴾ and (إِنَّا).

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾.
It is put in the jussive in our reading because of هل; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh because of the overt imperative, namely His saying (آمِنوا). The import of هل أدلكم is also a command in meaning, like your saying to a man: هل أنت ساكت؟ (will you be quiet?), whose meaning is: be quiet. And Allah knows best.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأُخْرَىٰ تُحِبُّونَهَا﴾.
It is in the position of the nominative, i.e.: and you have another [thing] in this world besides the reward of the Hereafter. Then He said: ﴿نَصْرٌ مِّن ٱللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ﴾, which explains the "other". Had it been نصرا من الله [in the accusative], it would have been correct; and had it been said: وآخر تحبونه, meaning the victory and the help, it would have been correct.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿كُونُوۤاْ أَنصَارَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd read it in the genitive construct, and the people of Medina read it: أنصاراً الله, leaving الأنصار unattached and not putting it in a construct. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: أنتم أنصار الله.
[Translator's note: «أنصاراً الله» is as printed; the Medinan reading is أنصاراً لله.]

farraa:2-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لاَ تَفْعَلُونَ﴾.
The Muslims used to say: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would do them, even if our lives and our wealth were lost in it. Then when the battle of Uḥud took place, they turned away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he was wounded in the head and his front tooth was broken; so He said: ﴿لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لاَ تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ because of that. Then He said: ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ [أَن تَقُولُواْ﴾. أن is in the position of the nominative, because كبر is like your saying: بئس رجلاً أخوك (how bad a man is your brother). And His saying: كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عند الله]: He has concealed in كبر a noun which is nominative. As for His saying ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلمة﴾, al-Ḥasan read it with the nominative [كلمةٌ], because he did not conceal anything [in the verb] and assigned the verb to كلمة; and whoever reads it in the accusative has concealed in كبرت a noun intended as nominative.

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهُم بُنْيَانٌ مَّرْصُوصٌ﴾: [joined] with lead (raṣāṣ); He is urging them to fight.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ﴾.
Yaḥyā or al-Aʿmash — al-Farrāʾ was unsure which — read it: "والله متمُّ نورِه" with the genitive construct (iḍāfa), and the people of the Ḥijāz read it with tanwīn: متمٌّ نورَه. Both are correct.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The clause «وهو العزيز» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the Divine Name.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: His words «لم»: the lām is a preposition; «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تقولون»; the alif of «ما» was omitted because it is preceded by a preposition; «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause «تقولون», the answer to the vocative, is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «كبر» is resumptive; «مقتا» is tamyīz (specification); the adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كبر»; and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أنْ» and what follows it is the fāʿil (agent) of «كبر».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «صفَّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «يقاتلون», and the clause «كأنهم بنيان» is a second ḥāl from the wāw in «يقاتلون».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The wāw is resumptive; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the implied verb «اذكر» (remember); the clause «لِمَ تؤذونني» is the answer to the vocative. The clause «وقد تعلمون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تؤذونني»; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أنَّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «علم»; the conditional clause is resumptive; and the clause «والله لا يهدي» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The wāw is a conjunction; «إذ» is an adverbial noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «إذ» in the previous verse; his words «يا بني»: one addressed in the vocative, a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun «إليكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رسول»; «مصدقا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسول الله»; the lām in «لما» is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening, and «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «مصدِّقًا»; «بين» is an adverb of place attached to the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); «مبشرا» is a noun conjoined to «مصدقا»; the preposition and its genitive noun «برسول» is attached to «مبشِّرا»; the clause «يأتي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول»; the clause «اسمه أحمد» is a second naʿt of «رسول»; the conditional clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «بالبينات» is attached to «جاءهم»; the clause «قالوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «ومن أظلم» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «ممن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أظلم»; the clause «وهو يُدعى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The object of «يريدون» is omitted, i.e.: they want the invalidation of the Qurʾān in order to extinguish; the clause «والله مُتِمُّ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يريدون»; the clause «ولو كره الكافرون» is a ḥāl clause from the pronoun in «مُتِمّ», and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it, i.e.: He perfected it and made it prevail; this wāw conjoins to an implied (muqaddar) ḥāl for exhaustiveness, i.e.: Allah perfects His light in every state, even in this state.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «ولو كره المشركون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The interrogative clause is resumptive, the answer to the vocative; the clause «تنجيكم» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «تؤمنون» is explicative of «التجارة»; the preposition and its genitive noun «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خير»; the clause «إن كنتم تعلمون» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «يغفر» is jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: if you believe, He will forgive you; «جنات» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: His words «وأخرى»: a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «تحبونها» is a naʿt (adjective); «نصر» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «أخرى»; the preposition and its genitive noun «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of it; and the clause «وبشِّر المؤمنين» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied (muqaddar) saying, i.e.: We said that to them with a saying like the saying of ʿĪsā; the preposition and its genitive noun «إلى الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ, i.e.: being, in the sense of turning towards Allah. The clause «قال» is resumptive; the clause «آمنت» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «من بني» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «طائفة»; and the clause «أيَّدْنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «كفرت».

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, كبر مقتا: accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)).
His saying أَن تَقولُوا: أن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate); its implied form is "your saying what you do not do is greatly hateful with Allah" (قولكم ما لا تفعلون كبر مقتا عند الله). It is also possible that أن is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is that you say" (هو أن تقولوا). In كبر there is an agent pronoun, i.e. "the hatefulness is great as hatefulness" (كبر المقت مقتا); this is among what is implied without prior mention, but it is implied on condition of explanation, so it is explained by مقت. It is good for كبر مقتا to be the khabar of the saying because it has the meaning of blame; its implied form is "your saying what you do not do is blameworthy", and His saying كبر مقتا has taken the place of "blameworthy" — just as you say زيد نعم رجلا ("Zayd, what an excellent man!"), putting زيد in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ with what follows it as its khabar, although there is nothing in it referring back to it; but it is permissible and good because its meaning is praise, so it is as if its implied form were "Zayd is praiseworthy", and your saying نعم رجلا has taken the place of "praiseworthy". So understand it.
His saying صفا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنيان: in the position of a ḥāl of the nominative latent pronoun in يقاتلون, i.e. they fight resembling a solid structure.
His saying وإذ قَالَ عِيسَى: the governing word in إذ is an implied verb, its implied form being "and remember when he said" (واذكر إذ قال).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying مُصدقا وَمُبشرا: two ḥāls (circumstantial) of ʿĪsā (Jesus), upon him be peace.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying تؤمنون بِاللَّه وتجاهدون: according to al-Mubarrad, its wording is the wording of a statement and its meaning is command, as if He said "believe and strive" (آمنوا وجاهدوا); for that reason He said يغفر لكم ويدخلكم in the jussive, because it is the apodosis of the command; so it is construed according to the meaning. What indicates that is that in the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is آمنوا, as a command. Others said: تؤمنون and تجاهدون are an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to what precedes it; it is as if, when He said, Exalted is He, هل أدلكم على تجارة, it was not known what the trade was, so He explained it by faith and striving, and it was known that the trade is faith and striving. On this view يغفر is the apodosis of the question, construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "Will you believe in Allah and strive? He will forgive you", since He has explained the trade by faith and striving, so it is the two of them, and it is as if they had been uttered in a position after هل; so the apodosis is construed according to that meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: يغفر is the apodosis of the question. If he meant this sense, it is good; if he did not mean it, that is not permissible, because forgiveness is not made necessary by the guidance (pointing out) — forgiveness is only made necessary by acceptance and action.
His saying وأخرى تحبونها: أخرى is in the position of the genitive by conjunction with تجارة, i.e. "shall I direct you to another trait which you love?"; this is the doctrine of al-Akhfash, and you put نصر in the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that is help" (ذلك نصر) or "it is help" (هي نصر). Al-Farrāʾ said أخرى is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the implied form according to him being "and you have another trait" (ولكم خلة أخرى); this is the choice of al-Ṭabarī, and he argued for it from His saying نصر وفتح in the nominative, as a badal (substitute) of أخرى.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying ظَاهِرين: accusative as the khabar (predicate) of أصبح, and the pronoun is its noun.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم﴾: سبح is a past verb; in لله the lām is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سبح﴾; it has also been said that the lām is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant); ما is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿في السماوات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted which is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿ما في الأرض﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ما في السماوات﴾; هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject); العزيز is the first khabar (predicate); and الحكيم is the second khabar.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون﴾: the lām is a preposition, and ما is an interrogative noun expressing disapproval and rebuke; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تقولون﴾; تقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لا is negative; and the clause تفعلون is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿كبر﴾: a past verb.
﴿مقتًا﴾: a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil (agent).
﴿عند الله﴾: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿مقتًا﴾, or a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿أن تقولوا﴾: أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; تقولوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن تقولوا﴾ is the fāʿil of ﴿كبر﴾.
﴿ما لا تفعلون﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لا is negative; and the clause ﴿لا تفعلون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is its noun (ism), and the clause يحب is its khabar (predicate); الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause يقاتلون has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; it is an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); في سبيله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقاتلون﴾; and صفًّا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in يقاتلون.
﴿كأنهم بنيان مرصوص﴾: كأن is an abrogating particle, ﴿هم﴾ is its noun, and بنيان is its khabar; مرصوص is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿بنيان﴾; and the clause is a second ḥāl, from the pronoun in ﴿صفًّا﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم لم تؤذونني وقد تعلمون أني رسول الله إليكم﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, the implied form being "remember when Mūsā said" (اذكر إذ قال موسى); the clause ﴿قال﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); موسى is the fāʿil (agent); لقومه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾; in لم the lām is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive by the lām — the reason for dropping the alif of interrogative ما when a preposition precedes it has already been given; تؤذونني is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); تعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; as for أني رسول الله: أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the yāʾ is its noun (ism), رسول is its khabar (predicate), and the Word of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; أن together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of تعلمون; إليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿رسول﴾; and the clause وقد تعلمون … etc. is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning: whoever venerates Allah venerates His Messenger.
﴿فلما زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is linking (rābiṭa) or temporal (ḥīniyya); زاغوا is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause أزاغ الله قلوبهم has no grammatical position; الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وإذ قال عيسى ابن مريم يا بني إسرائيل إني رسول الله إليكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إذ﴾ is conjoined to ﴿إذ﴾ in the previous verse; the clause ﴿قال﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); عيسى is the fāʿil (agent); ابن مريم is a badal (substitute) from عيسى; يا بني إسرائيل is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the yāʾ is its noun (ism), and رسول الله إليكم is its khabar (predicate); and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿مصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ومبشرًا برسول يأتي من بعدي اسمه أحمد﴾: مصدقًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun concealed in رسول الله, since it is interpreted as "one sent" (مرسل); لما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مصدقًا﴾. ﴿بين﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. يدي is muḍāf ilayhi, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a dual; مبشرًا is conjoined to ﴿مصدقًا﴾, so it is a ḥāl like it; برسول is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مبشرًا﴾; the clause يأتي is an adjective (ṣifa) of رسول; من بعدي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يأتي﴾; اسمه is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أحمد its khabar; and the clause is a second adjective.
﴿فلما جاءهم بالبينات قالوا هذا سحر مبين﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; لما is linking (rābiṭa) or temporal (ḥīniyya); جاءهم is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بالبينات is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿جاءهم﴾; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position; the clause هذا سحر مبين, made of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the object of their saying; and the clause ﴿فلما جاءهم...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ومن أظلم ممن افترى﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; من is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, i.e. "no one", in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); أظلم is the khabar (predicate); ممن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أظلم﴾; and the clause افترى is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿على الله﴾: على is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿افترى﴾.
﴿الكذب﴾: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وهو يدعى إلى الإسلام﴾: the wāw is for the ḥāl (circumstantial); هو is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يدعى is the khabar of هو; the clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl; يدعى is an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named); and إلى الإسلام is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يدعى﴾.
﴿والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين﴾: الله is the mubtadaʾ, and the clause لا يهدي is the khabar; القوم is the mafʿūl bihi; and الظالمين is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿القوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم﴾: يريدون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); in ﴿ليطفئوا﴾ the lām is for cause (taʿlīl), and يطفئوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw of the group is in the position of a nominative as fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar from the implied ﴿أن﴾ and the imperfect verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the lām with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يريدون﴾; the object of يريدون is omitted, the implied form being "they want fabrication, in order to extinguish the light of Allah". Or the lām in ﴿ليطفئوا﴾ is a connective (ṣila) for emphasis that has entered upon the object, and يطفئوا is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يطفئوا﴾ is the object of يريد, the implied form being "they want the extinguishing of the light of Allah". ﴿نور﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the fatḥa, and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); بأفواههم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يطفئوا﴾, and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿يطفئوا﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī), the implied ﴿أن﴾; and the clause ﴿يريدون...﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive.
﴿والله متم نوره ولو كره الكافرون﴾: the wāw is for the ḥāl (circumstantial); الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject); متم is the khabar (predicate); نوره is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يريدون, or of يطفئوا; the wāw is also for the ḥāl; لو is conditional; كره الكافرون is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl from the preceding ḥāl clause, so they are nested (mutadākhila); and the apodosis of ﴿لو﴾ is omitted, the implied form being "He would complete it and make it manifest".

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿هو الذي أرسل رسوله﴾: هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and الذي is its khabar (predicate); the clause أرسل is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. رسوله is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿بالهدى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسل﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ودين الحق﴾: conjoined to الهدى.
﴿ليظهره على الدين كله﴾: the lām is for cause (taʿlīl); يظهره is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿أرسل﴾; على الدين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يظهره﴾; and كله is a tawkīd (emphasis).
﴿ولو كره المشركون﴾: the clause is a ḥāl; the object of كره is omitted, i.e. "its being made manifest"; and the apodosis of لو is also omitted, the implied form being "He would make it manifest".

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿هل أدلكم﴾: هل is an interrogative particle; أدلكم is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I" (أنا), and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿على تجارة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أدلكم﴾.
﴿تنجيكم من عذاب أليم﴾: the clause تنجيكم is an adjective of ﴿تجارة﴾; من عذاب is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تنجيكم﴾; and أليم is an adjective of ﴿عذاب﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿تؤمنون بالله ورسوله وتجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالكم وأنفسكم﴾: the clause is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or resumptive in answer to a supplied question, and it has no grammatical position; تؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), but it has the sense of a command; in بالله the bāʾ is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تؤمنون﴾; رسوله is conjoined to بالله; تجاهدون is conjoined to تؤمنون; في سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجاهدون﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); بأموالكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجاهدون﴾; and أنفسكم is conjoined to أموالكم.
﴿ذلكم خير لكم﴾: ذلكم is the mubtadaʾ, خير is the khabar, and لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خير.
﴿إن كنتم تعلمون﴾: إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause تعلمون is the khabar of كنتم; the apodosis of the conditional is omitted, its implied form being "then do it" (فافعلوه); and the object of تعلمون is omitted for brevity since it is known, i.e. "that it is better for you".

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿يغفر لكم ذنوبكم﴾: يغفر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of a supplied condition; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو); لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يغفر﴾; ذنوبكم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of the supplied condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
﴿ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يدخلكم is conjoined to يغفر; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جنات﴾; من تحتها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجري﴾; and الأنهار is the fāʿil.
﴿ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; مساكن is conjoined to جنات; طيبة is a naʿt of ﴿مساكن﴾; and في جنات عدن is a second naʿt.
﴿ذلك الفوز العظيم﴾: ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the forgiveness and the admission into the gardens; الفوز is the khabar (predicate); and العظيم is a naʿt of ﴿الفوز﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وأخرى تحبونها نصر من الله وفتح قريب وبشر المؤمنين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أخرى is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "He will give you another blessing" (يؤتكم نعمة أخرى), and the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿يغفر لكم﴾; تحبون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), but it has the sense of a command [Translator's note: so in the source; this remark seems carried over from تؤمنون in verse 11, and تحبونها here is descriptive, not a command]; the hāʾ is a pronoun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أخرى﴾; نصر is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that other blessing is help from Allah", or a badal (substitute) from أخرى if you parse it as a mubtadaʾ; من الله is a naʿt of ﴿نصر﴾; فتح is conjoined to نصر; and قريب is a naʿt. وبشر: the wāw is a conjunction, and بشر is an imperative verb, conjoined to تؤمنون because that has the sense of a command; and المؤمنين is the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿كونوا أنصار الله﴾: كونوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb; the wāw is its noun (ism); أنصار الله is its khabar (predicate); and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿كما قال عيسى ابن مريم للحواريين﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); ﴿ما﴾ is a maṣdar-forming particle; ﴿قال﴾ is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; عيسى is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma; ﴿ابن﴾ is a naʿt (adjective), nominative by the ḍamma; ﴿مريم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the fatḥa because it is a diptote; ﴿للحواريين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾; the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) ﴿ما﴾; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما قال﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive.
﴿من أنصاري إلى الله﴾: من is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); أنصاري is the khabar, nominative by the implied ḍamma, in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently something like "and the yāʾ is" has dropped out — it is the yāʾ of the first person that is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi]; إلى الله is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ of the first person, on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "turning towards the support of Allah"; and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿قال الحواريون﴾: a verb and its fāʿil.
﴿نحن أنصار الله﴾: نحن is the mubtadaʾ and أنصار الله the khabar; the clause is the object of the saying; and it is a case of annexing a descriptive noun to its object.
﴿فآمنت طائفة من بني إسرائيل وكفرت طائفة﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to omitted clauses that must be supplied, i.e. "so when ʿĪsā was raised to heaven, the people split into two groups over him, and a party believed"; طائفة is the fāʿil of آمنت; من بني إسرائيل is a naʿt of ﴿طائفة﴾; and كفرت طائفة is conjoined to فآمنت طائفة.
﴿فأيدنا الذين آمنوا على عدوهم﴾: the fāʾ also conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "so the two parties fought"; أيدنا is a verb and its fāʿil; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and على عدوهم is attached to ﴿أيدنا﴾.
﴿فأصبحوا ظاهرين﴾: فأصبحوا is conjoined to ﴿فأيدنا﴾; the wāw is its noun, and ظاهرين is its khabar.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: His saying سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ, i.e. whatever He, Majestic and Mighty, willed submitted to Him and yielded; so everything is included in this, because ما is general in the speech of the Arabs. وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ in His retribution on whoever disobeys Him. الْحَكِيمُ in His management [of affairs].

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: لِمَ: the original is لما; the alif is dropped because of the word's being joined to what precedes it and because it is interrogative.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: مَقْتاً is accusative as an explanation (bayān) [Translator's note: i.e. tamyīz (specification)], and the agent is implied in كبر, i.e. "that saying is grievous". أَنْ تَقُولُوا ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ: «أن» is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), or on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ. What results from this is that no one should say anything except what he firmly intends to do, and he should say "if Allah wills", lest he be cut off [by death] before it.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
Love from Him, Majestic and Mighty, is the acceptance of knowledge [Translator's note: so in the source, العلم; presumably العمل, "the deed", as in the parallel phrase at 60:7] and rewarding it. صَفًّا is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is said:
by this He showed that fighting in the way of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, with a person on foot is better than on a mount.
كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ i.e. it has been made firm and well-wrought, so nothing in it projects beyond anything else; and it is said:
مرصوص means built with lead (raṣāṣ).
