nahhas-irab:5-5.t: وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ i.e. and remember. يا قَوْمِ لِمَ تُؤْذُونَنِي: a vocative in construct, and the yāʾ is dropped because the vocative is a place of omission. وَقَدْ تَعْلَمُونَ أَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ: the original is أنّني. فَلَمَّا زاغُوا i.e. they swerved from the truth. أَزاغَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ as requital for their deed; and it is said: He caused their hearts to swerve from the reward. وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ i.e. He does not grant success in what is right to whoever goes out from faith to disbelief. It is narrated from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may Allah be pleased with him, and Abū Umāma that these are the Ḥarūriyya.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
I.e. and remember this. مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise وَمُبَشِّراً بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ. This [Translator's note: i.e. مِنْ بَعْدِيَ with the yāʾ given fatḥa] is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr; and the reading of Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī is من بعد اسمه أحمد, dropping the yāʾ in continuous speech because of its being quiescent and the sīn after it being quiescent. This is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, and he argued for dropping it that when you begin you say:
اسمه, giving the hamza kasra. This is an argument from which no sense results. The view on this among the scholars of Arabic is that this is the yāʾ of the first person: some Arabs give it fatḥa and some make it quiescent; it has been read with both these readings, and both are correct — except that it is more common for the first-person yāʾ to be given a vowel when a quiescent letter comes after it, so that it does not fall away, and to be made quiescent when a vowelled letter comes after it; and in each of the two cases what is permissible in the other is permissible. فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ i.e. when Aḥmad came to them with clear signs, i.e. with proofs and dazzling signs, قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: I.e. and who does greater wrong than one who said of whoever came to him with clear signs: "He is a sorcerer", and "this is manifest sorcery", i.e. manifest to whoever sees it as sorcery. وَهُوَ يُدْعى إِلَى الْإِسْلامِ: and when he is invited to Islam he says: "this is manifest sorcery". The reading of Ṭalḥa is وهو يدّعي إلى الإسلام. وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ: they are those who say of the clear signs: "this is manifest sorcery".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِؤُا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ i.e. by this saying of theirs. وَاللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ i.e. completing Islam and raising it high. This [Translator's note: i.e. مُتِمٌّ نُورَهُ, with tanwīn, as the following remark implies; the print shows the construct] is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; and Ibn Kathīr, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read متمّ نوره [in construct]. The original is the tanwīn, and the omission is for lightness. وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكافِرُونَ: and the object is omitted.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: The view of Abū Hurayra on this is that it will be when the Messiah ﷺ descends and the whole religion has become the religion of Islam.

nahhas-irab:10-13.t:
Qatāda said: had He not made clear the trade, it would have been sought. He said: تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ. Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān used to hold this view and say: «تؤمنون» is by way of ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) that resembles the badal (substitute). He related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that the meaning of «تؤمنون» is "believe!", by way of obligation. Abū l-ʿAbbās said: the proof of that is يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ, jussive because it is the response to the command, and conjoined to it is وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ.
As for the view of al-Akhfash Saʿīd that وَأُخْرى is in the position of a genitive on the basis that it is conjoined to تجارة, it is permissible; but sounder than it is the view of al-Farrāʾ that «أخرى» is in the position of a nominative in the sense of "and you have another"; what shows that is نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ in the nominative, and they are not genitive; and according to the view of al-Akhfash the nominative is by an implied mubtadaʾ. وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ i.e. with the help and the victory. Al-naṣr in the language is assistance.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا أَنْصارَ اللَّهِ [Translator's note: i.e. أَنْصاراً لِلَّهِ, with tanwīn, as the following remarks require; the print shows the construct form] is the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr; and the Kufans read كُونُوا أَنْصارَ اللَّهِ in construct. This is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, and his argument for it is قالَ الْحَوارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنْصارُ اللَّهِ, and they did not say أنصار الله [Translator's note: i.e. أنصارا لله]. This argument is not binding, because the two differ: the first is "be among those who help Allah", so its meaning is indefinite, and so it ought to be أنصارا لله, though the construct is permissible in it, i.e. "be those of whom this is said"; while the meaning of the second is definite. Do you not see that when you say فلان ناصر لله its meaning is "among those who do this", and when you make it definite its meaning is "the one known for this", as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 483-
هو الجواد الذي يعطيك نائله ... حينا ويظلم أحيانا فيظّلم
(He is the generous one who gives you his gift at one time, and at times is imposed upon and bears it)
 As for the view of al-Qutabī that the meaning of مَنْ أَنْصارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ is "with Allah", it is not sound: قمت إلى زيد is not permissible in the sense of "with Zayd". Abū Jaʿfar said: its implied meaning is "who will join his help of me to Allah's help of me?" فَآمَنَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ وَكَفَرَتْ طائِفَةٌ: we have explained it. Mujāhid said: فَأَيَّدْنَا — so We strengthened. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said concerning the meaning of فَأَيَّدْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلى عَدُوِّهِمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا ظاهِرِينَ: Allah supported them [with] Muḥammad ﷺ [Translator's note: the source reads أيّدهم الله محمد, apparently for بمحمد], and his confirming to them that ʿĪsā ﷺ is the Word of Allah.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is redundant (zāʾida). (يطفئوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām. (بأفواههم) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يطفئوا), and (الباء) is for instrumentality. (الواو) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) wāw in both places. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يطفئوا) is in the position of an accusative direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of a verb of wanting.
The clause «يريدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يطفئوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (أن), which is implied.
The clause «اللَّه متمّ ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يريدون - or of يطفئوا. The clause «لو كره الكافرون ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun in متمّ. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "even if the disbelievers dislike the light of Allah, Allah is the One who brings forth His light and makes it manifest."

* Morphology:
(متمّ) is an active participle from the quadriliteral verb أتمّ; its pattern is مفعل, and its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.

* Rhetoric:
The representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya) in the words of Allah the Exalted يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِؤُا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ.
It depicts their state, in their striving to nullify the truth, as the state of one who blows at the sun with his mouth to extinguish it, in mockery and derision of them, as people say: "He is extinguishing the very eye of the sun."
Some eminent scholars held that what is meant by the light of Allah is His true religion, by way of explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), and likewise in the words of Allah the Exalted وَاللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(بالهدى) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of أرسل or from its object. (اللام) is for causation. (يظهره) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (على الدين) is attached to (يظهره), the verb being given the sense of "make it prevail" (يعليه). (الواو) is a ḥāl wāw. (لو كره المشركون) is like لو كره الكافرون [Note: in the previous verse (8).].
The clause «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أرسل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «يظهره ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن), which is implied.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يظهره..) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (أرسل); the agent of يظهر is a pronoun referring to the word of majesty (Allah).
The clause «لو كره المشركون» is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يظهره.

safi-cedvel:10-13.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has been given [Note: in verse (2) of this sūra.]. (هل) is an interrogative particle. (على تجارة) is attached to (أدلّ). (من عذاب) is attached to (تنجيكم).
The clause «يأيّها الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هل أدلّكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative (jawāb al-nidāʾ).
The clause «تنجيكم ... » is in the position of a genitive naʿt (adjective) of تجارة.
11- (باللَّه) is attached to (تؤمنون). (في سبيل) is attached to (تجاهدون), and likewise (بأموالكم). The demonstrative in (ذلكم) refers to faith and striving. (لكم) is attached to (خير). (كنتم) is a defective past verb (kāna) in the position of the jussive, being the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «تؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or it is an explication, according to Ibn Hishām, explaining "the trade".].
The clause «تجاهدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تؤمنون.
The clause «ذلكم خير ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «كنتم تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تعلمون ... » is in the position of an accusative khabar (predicate) of كنتم. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "then believe and strive ..."
12- (يغفر) is a jussive imperfect verb, the apodosis of an implied condition. (لكم) is attached to (يغفر). (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري) [Note: with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "beneath its trees"; it is also possible that the prepositional phrase is attached to a ḥāl from الأنهار.]. (مساكن) is conjoined to جنّات, and tanwīn is withheld from it because it is a plural of the form of the ultimate plurals (muntahā al-jumūʿ). (في جنّات) is attached to a second adjective of مساكن. The demonstrative in (ذلك) refers to the forgiveness and the entry into the Gardens.
The clause «يغفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined by fāʾ, i.e. "if you do it, He will forgive."
The clause «يدخلكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يغفر.
The clause «ذلك الفوز ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
13- (الواو) is a conjunction. (أخرى) is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "He will give you another blessing" (يؤتكم نعمة أخرى), jussive by conjunction to (يغفر) [Note: or it is omitted on the pattern of ishtighāl, i.e. "you love another"; it is also possible that (أخرى) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is نصر من الله, or that it is conjoined to تجارة and genitive like it.]. (نصر) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي" (it), i.e. the other blessing. (من اللَّه) is attached to (نصر). (الواو) is resumptive - or a conjunction. The clause « (يؤتكم) أخرى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يغفر.
The clause «تحبّونها ... » is in the position of an accusative naʿt of أخرى.
The clause « (هي) نصر ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «بشر المؤمنين» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Benefits:
- Conjoining a declarative (khabar) onto an imperative/performative (inshāʾ), and the reverse: most scholars forbade it, among them Ibn Mālik and Ibn ʿUṣfūr, while al-Ṣaffār and a group permitted it, citing the words of Allah the Exalted:
«فَاتَّقُوا النَّارَ الَّتِي وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجارَةُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكافِرِينَ وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ» and His words in Sūrat al-Ṣaff, in the very verse we are dealing with: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى تِجارَةٍ تُنْجِيكُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ. تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ، يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ وَمَساكِنَ طَيِّبَةً فِي جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ، وَأُخْرى تُحِبُّونَها نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ).
This position, namely the permissibility of conjoining a declarative onto an imperative, is supported by the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وإن شفائي عبرة مهراقة ... وهل عند رسم دارس من معوّل
(Indeed my cure is a tear that is poured out ... and is there, at a worn-out trace of a dwelling, anything to rely on?)
al-Zamakhsharī rejected [the evidence of] the two verses, of al-Baqara and al-Ṣaff, denying the permissibility of conjoining a declarative onto an imperative. He said: As for the verse of al-Baqara, the imperative is not what the conjunction relies on, so that a match would be sought for it; rather, what is meant is to conjoin the clause of the reward of the believers onto the clause of the punishment of the disbelievers, as you say: "Zayd is punished with the shackle, and give glad tidings to so-and-so of release." He also allowed it to be conjoined to اتقوا. More complete than his words in the first answer is to say: What the conjunction relies on is the clause of reward, as he mentioned, and to this it may be added: the discourse is looked at for the meaning resulting from it, as if it had been said: "Those who believe and do righteous deeds have Gardens, so give them glad tidings of that." As for the second answer, it is open to question, because it cannot be an apodosis of the condition, since the command to give glad tidings is not conditional on the disbelievers' inability to produce the like of the Qur'an. The reply is: it is known that they are not the believers, so it is as if it had been said: "If they do not do so, give glad tidings of the Gardens to others" - the meaning being: give these obstinate ones the news that they have no share in Paradise.
And he said regarding the verse of al-Ṣaff: the conjunction is onto (تؤمنون) because it has the sense of "believe" (آمنوا). It does no harm that the one addressed by (تؤمنون) is the believers and by (بشر) the Prophet, peace be upon him, nor that it be said of (تؤمنون) that it is an explication of the trade and not a request, and that (يغفر لكم) is the answer to the question, the cause being placed in the position of the effect; for difference of agents does no harm, as in our saying "Stand, and you, Zayd, sit"; and because (تؤمنون) is not necessarily an explication. Granting that, it is still possible that it is an explication while being a command, in that the meaning of the preceding discourse would be "trade a trade that will save you from a painful punishment", as (فهل أنتم منتهون) was in the sense of "desist"; or that it is an explication in meaning and not in technical form, because a command may be conveyed to give the meaning obtained from the explicative particle. One says: "Shall I direct you to the cause of your salvation? Believe in Allah", just as you say "It is that you believe in Allah." In that case the conjunction is impossible, since giving glad tidings does not enter into the meaning of the explication.

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has been given [Note: in verse (2) of this sūra.]. (ما) is a maṣdar particle. (للحواريّين) is attached to (قال).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما قال..) is in the position of a genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "We said that, like the saying of ʿĪsā" [Note: al-Zamakhsharī, in his i'rab of the noble verse, took a course that changes the meaning of the verse, i.e.: "Be helpers of Allah as the disciples were helpers of ʿĪsā when he said to them: Who are my helpers toward Allah?"].
(من) is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ, its khabar being (أنصاري). (إلى اللَّه) is attached to a ḥāl from the first-person pronoun, i.e. "turning toward helping Allah", that is, with an omitted muḍāf. (الفاء) is resumptive. (من بني) is attached to an adjective of طائفة. The second (الفاء) is a conjunction. (على عدوّهم) is attached to (أيّدنا), the verb being given the sense of "We strengthened" (قوّينا). (الفاء) is a conjunction ...
The clause «النداء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «كونوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause « (قلنا) ذلك كقول ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «قال عيسى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).
The clause «من أنصاري ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قال الحواريّون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «نحن أنصار اللَّه ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «آمنت طائفة ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or the clause is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "when ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, was raised to heaven, the people split into groups, and a group believed ..."].
The clause «كفرت طائفة ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آمنت طائفة.
The clause «أيّدنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كفرت طائفة.
The clause «آمنوا (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أصبحوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أيّدنا....

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(للَّه) attached to a ḥāl from the relative» , (في السموات) attached to an omitted element, ṣila of the relative, and likewise (في الأرض), ṣila of the second relative (الواو) circumstantial «2» ..
Clause: «سبّح للَّه ما في السموات ... » has no grammatical position, initial.
Clause: «هو العزيز ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from the divine name «3».

safi-cedvel:2-3.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) the one addressed, a specific indefinite, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative (الذين) badal from أيّ, in the position of accusative - or ʿaṭf bayān of it - (لم) attached to (تقولون), and (ما) is interrogative, its alif deleted, (ما) relative [Note: or an indefinite noun described, meaning "something", its returning pronoun omitted.
(2, 3) or in the position of accusative, naʿt of (ما).] in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi, its returning pronoun omitted (لا) negative (مقتا) tamyīz, accusative (أن) a maṣdar and accusative particle (عند) accusative adverbial attached to (كبر) ...
Clause: «النداء ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative (الذين).
Clause: «تقولون ... » has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
Clause: «لا تفعلون ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative (ما) «2».
Clause: «كبر ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «تقولوا ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقولوا..) is in the position of nominative, fāʿil of كبر.
Clause: «لا تفعلون (the second) ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of (ما) «3».

* Rhetoric:
Hyperbole and repetition: in the saying of the Exalted كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ تَقُولُوا ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ.
This is among the most eloquent and most rhetorically effective speech. Its meaning aims at astonishment without the form of astonishment, to magnify the matter in the hearts of the hearers, because astonishment arises only at something that departs from its like and kind. The verb was predicated of «أَنْ تَقُولُوا» and «مقتا» was put in the accusative as its specification, indicating that their saying what they do not do is pure hatred with no admixture, owing to the extent to which hatred is rooted in it. The word "hatred" (maqt) was chosen because it is the most intense and most forceful of the words for aversion; it did not stop at making the aversion great, but made it its most intense and most abominable, and "with Allah" is more forceful than that.
Beyond these four aspects there is a fifth: the repetition of «ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ», a single expression in a single speech; among the benefits of repetition are inspiring dread and magnification. Otherwise the speech was complete without it.

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(في سبيله) attached to (يقاتلون), (صفّا) ḥāl from the fāʿil in (يقاتلون) ..
Clause: «إنّ اللَّه يحبّ ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «يحبّ ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of إنّ.
Clause: «يقاتلون ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative (الذين).
Clause: «كأنّهم بنيان ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from the pronoun in (صفّا).

* Morphology:
(مرصوص), a passive participle from the triliteral (رصّ); its wazn is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
The inclusion of the specific within the general: the general prohibition came first in the third verse, then immediately after this general prohibition came the saying of the Exalted إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ.
Mentioning this directly after the general prohibition is evidence that the hatred was attached to the saying of those who had promised steadfastness in fighting the unbelievers and did not fulfil it, as you say to one who has committed a particular offence:
"Do not do what attaches shame to you, and do not curse Zayd." The benefit of such an arrangement is: prohibiting one thing twice, included in the general and singled out in particular, which is better than prohibiting it in particular twice, for that is counted as mere repetition, whereas this is repetition together with the magnification and dread that generalization carries.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (لقومه) attached to (قال), (قوم) the one addressed, a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the omitted yāʾ, omitted for lightness.
And it (the yāʾ) is muḍāf ilayhi (لم) attached to (تؤذونني), and (ما) is interrogative, its alif deleted (الواو) circumstantial (قد) for certainty [Note: that is, because of the certainty of their knowledge of his message; so it is neither for reduction nor for approximation.], (إليكم) attached to (رسول).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّي رسول ... ) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of تعلمون.
(الفاء) resumptive (لمّا) an adverbial meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, attached to the apodosis أزاغ (الواو) resumptive (لا) negative.
Clause: «قال موسى ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «النداء ... » is in the position of accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «تؤذونني ... » has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
Clause: «تعلمون ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from the fāʿil of تؤذونني.
Clause: «زاغوا ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «أزاغ اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «اللَّه لا يهدي ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (اللَّه).

* Morphology:
(أزاغ), it has an iʿlāl whose rule is like the rule of the iʿlāl in زاغ.. See verse (17) of Sūrat al-Najm.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(وإذ قال عيسى) like وإذ قال موسى «1», (ابن) badal from عيسى, nominative [Note: or ʿaṭf bayān of it, or naʿt of it.], (إليكم) attached to (رسول) (مصدّقا) ḥāl from the pronoun in رسول (لما) attached to (مصدّقا) [Note: or the lām is redundant for strengthening, and ما is in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi of the active participle (مصدقا).], (بين) accusative adverbial attached to an omitted element, ṣila of ما (من التوراة) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in the omitted ṣila (برسول) attached to (مبشّرا), (من بعدي) attached to (يأتي), (فلما جاءهم) like لمّا زاغوا «4», and the fāʿil of جاءهم is a pronoun referring to Aḥmad [Note: the pronoun may refer to ʿĪsā, peace be upon him.], (بالبيّنات) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of جاءهم.
Clause: «قال عيسى ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «النداء ... » is in the position of accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «إنّي رسول ... » has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
Clause: «يأتي ... » is in the position of genitive, naʿt of رسول.
Clause: «اسمه احمد» is in the position of genitive, second naʿt of رسول [Note: or in the position of accusative, ḥāl from the fāʿil of يأتي - or from رسول.]
Clause: «جاءهم ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «هذا سحر ... » is in the position of accusative, the quoted speech.

* Morphology:
(أحمد), a proper noun, one of the names of the Messenger, peace be upon him, taken from al-ḥamd (praise); it is of the form of the imperfect beginning with the hamza of the first person, so it is a diptote (denied tanwīn).

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (من) an interrogative noun in the sense of denial, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ, its khabar being (أظلم), (ممّن) attached to (أظلم) (على اللَّه) attached to (افترى), (الكذب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: or mafʿūl muṭlaq, standing in for the maṣdar because it meets it in meaning.], (الواو) circumstantial (إلى الإسلام) attached to (يدعى), (الواو) resumptive (لا) negative.
Clause: «من أظلم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «افترى ... » has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative (من).
Clause: «هو يدعى ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl.
Clause: «يدعى ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
Clause: «اللَّه لا يهدي ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Clause: «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (اللَّه).

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {كَبُرَ مَقْتاً}: there are several possibilities. The first is that it belongs to the chapter of niʿma and biʾsa (verbs of praise and blame), so that «كَبُرَ» contains a vague latent pronoun explained by the indefinite noun after it. «وأَنْ تقولوا» is the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm), and so the well-known disagreement arises regarding it: is its nominative ending by virtue of being a mubtadaʾ, with its khabar being the clause preceding it, or is its khabar omitted, or is it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as was set out earlier. This is a regular rule: every verb at which wonder (taʿajjub) is permissible may be built on the pattern faʿula with ḍamma on the ʿayn, and it follows niʿma and biʾsa in all rulings. The second is that it is one of the forms of wonder. Ibn ʿUṣfūr counted it among the wonder constructions given a chapter in grammar, saying: "The form mā afʿalahu, afʿil bihi, and la-faʿula, such as لَرَمُوَ الرجل." Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, saying: "This is among the most eloquent speech and the most expressive in its meaning. By «كَبُرَ» he intended wonder, though not in its own wording, as in his saying:
4256 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . .
غلَتْ نابٌ كُلَيْبٌ بَواؤُها
(How costly became the she-camel Kulayb's equivalent!)
Then he said: "It was predicated of «أَنْ تقولوا», and «مَقْتاً» was put in the accusative as its explanation, indicating that their saying what they do not do is pure hatred, with no admixture in it." The third is that «كَبُرَ» is neither for wonder nor for blame, but is predicated of «أَنْ تقولوا», and «مَقْتاً» is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from agency, the original being: كَبُرَ مَقْتُ أَنْ يقولوا, that is, "the hatred of your saying grew great." It is also possible that the agent is a latent pronoun referring to the maṣdar understood from his saying «لِم تقولونَ», that is, "it grew great", meaning the saying, "in hatred"; and «أَنْ تقولوا» on this view is either a badal (substitute) for that pronoun, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is "it is that you say". Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُقاتَلون» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, in the passive. «يُقَتَّلون» was also read, with shadda.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {صَفّاً}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "in ranks" or "drawn up in ranks".
His saying: {كَأَنَّهُم}: it may be a second ḥāl from the agent of «يُقاتِلون»; it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «صَفّاً», in which case it is a nested ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila); al-Zamakhsharī said this. It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «صَفَّاً»; al-Ḥawfī said this. The pronoun returned to «صَفّاً» in the plural because it is a plural in meaning, as in His saying {وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنين اقتتلوا} [al-Ḥujurāt: 9]. As for «المَرْصُوص», it was said: that whose parts are fitted together and level. It was also said: that which is bound with lead. It was also said: it is from close-packing, from the tight set of the teeth (tarāṣṣ al-asnān). Al-Rāʿī said:
4257 - ما لَقِيَ البيضُ من الحُرْقوصِ ... يَفْتَحُ بابَ المُغْلَقِ المَرْصوصِ
(What the fair ones have suffered from the ḥurqūṣ, which opens the door of the shut, tightly-fitted [place].)
الحُرْقوص is a small crawling creature that is fond of virgin women.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {وَقَد تَّعْلَمُونَ}: a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya).

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {مُّصَدِّقاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise «مُبَشِّراً»; the governor is «رسول» because it has the sense of "one sent" (al-mursal). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask, by what are «مُصَدِّقاً» and «مُبَشِّراً» put in the accusative: by the sense of sending contained in «الرسول», or by «إليكم»? I say: by the sense of sending; because «إليكم» is a ṣila of «الرسول», so it cannot govern anything, since prepositions do not govern by themselves but by the verbal sense they contain; so when they occur as ṣilas that do not implicate a verbal sense, from where would they govern?" End. By his saying "ṣilas" he means that they are attached to «رسول» as a connection to it, that is, their meaning is connected with it, not the technical ṣila. «يأتي مِنْ بعدي» and «اسمُه أحمدُ» are two clauses in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول»; or «اسمُه أحمدُ» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «يَأْتي»; or the first is a naʿt and the second a ḥāl. That the two be ḥāls is weak because they come from an indefinite, although Sībawayh permits it. «أحمدُ» may be a transfer from the imperfect verb or from the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), the apparent one being the second. On either view it is barred from the ṣarf (is a diptote) because of being a proper name and the predominant verbal pattern, except that on the first it is barred when definite and takes tanwīn when indefinite, while on the second it is barred whether definite or indefinite, since the adjectival quality replaces the proper-name quality. When it is made indefinite after having been a proper name, the disagreement between Sībawayh and al-Akhfash arises, which is a well-known question among the grammarians. Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him, recited, praising the Prophet ﷺ, and he gave it tanwīn:
4258 - صلَّى الإِلهُ ومَنْ يَحُفُّ بعرشِه ... والطيبونَ على المباركِ أحمدِ
(God blessed, and those who surround His throne, and the pure ones, the blessed Aḥmad.)
«أحمد» is a badal or a bayān (explicative apposition) of «المبارك».
His saying: {هذا سِحْرٌ}: the disagreement of the readers regarding it has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida.
And the Shaykh said here: "The majority read «سِحْرٌ», while ʿAbd Allāh, Ṭalḥa, al-Aʿmash and Ibn Wathāb read «ساحر»," and he omitted mention of the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī].

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {وَهُوَ يدعى إِلَى الإسلام}: a circumstantial clause from the agent of «افترى»; this is the reading of the majority. Ṭalḥa read «يَدَّعي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and shadda on the dāl, in the active, and there are two interpretations of it. One is that of al-Zamakhsharī, namely that yafta ʿilu is in the sense of yafʿalu, like لَمَسَه and التمَسه. The two pronouns, I mean «هو» and the latent one in «يَدَّعي», refer to Allah the Exalted, and then the two readings are of one meaning, as if it had been said: "and Allah calls to Islam." In the first reading the two pronouns refer to «مَنْ». The second is that it is from ادَّعى كذا دَعْوَى, but since «يَدَّعي» was made to imply the sense of "to belong to, to be affiliated with", it was made transitive with «إلى», otherwise it is transitive by itself; and on this view the two pronouns are also for «مَنْ», as in the well-known reading.
From Ṭalḥa also: «يُدَّعى» with shadda on the dāl, in the passive. Al-Zamakhsharī explained it according to what was said before: ادَّعاه and دَعاه are of one meaning, like لَمَسه and التمَسه. The two pronouns refer to «مَنْ», the reverse of what he held in explaining the first reading, in which the two pronouns refer to Allah the Exalted, as was set out earlier.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لِيُطْفِئُواْ}: there are several possibilities regarding this lām. The first is that it is added (mazīda) to the object of "wanting". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its original is: they want to extinguish (yurīdūna an yuṭfiʾū), as came in Sūrat al-Tawba. It is as if this lām was added to the verb of wanting for emphasis, because of the sense of wanting in it, as in your saying «جِئتُ لأكرمَك», just as the lām was added in «لا أبالك» to emphasize the sense of iḍāfa in «لا أباك»." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The lām in «لِيُطْفِئوا» is an emphasizing lām that entered the object, for the implied form is: they want to extinguish. This lām most often accompanies the object when it is fronted. You say: «لزيدٍ ضَرَبْتُ» and «لِرؤيتِك قصَدْتُ»." End. This is not the position of Sībawayh and most people. Moreover, Abū Muḥammad's saying "most often accompanies..." to the end is not apparent, because no one says it is obligatory at all; rather its addition is permissible, and it is also not the case that its addition is the more frequent; rather its absence is more frequent.
The second is that it is the lām of cause, and the object is omitted, that is: they want to nullify the Qur'ān, or repel Islam, or destroy the Messenger, peace be upon him, in order to extinguish.
The third is that it has the sense of the subjunctive «أَنْ», and that it governs the verb itself. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The Arabs put the lām of purpose (lām kay) in the place of «أَنْ» with arāda and amara"; and al-Kisāʾī too held this. A similar case was given for you in His saying {يُرِيدُ الله لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ} in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ [verse 26].
His saying: {مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Ḥafṣ and Ibn Kathīr read it with «مُتِمُّ» in iḍāfa to «نورِه»; the rest read it with tanwīn and «نورَه» in the accusative. The iḍāfa is a lightening, and the tanwīn is the original. The Shaykh disputes that it is the original, as was given earlier. His saying «واللَّهُ متمُّ» is a circumstantial clause from the agent of «يريدون» or «يُطفئوا»; and his saying «ولو كَرِه» is a ḥāl from this ḥāl, so the two are nested. The apodosis of «لو» is omitted, that is, "He would complete it and make it prevail", and likewise {وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الكافرون}.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {تُنجِيكُم}: the clause is a ṣifa (qualifier) of «تجارة». Ibn ʿĀmir read «تُنْجِّيكم» with shadda; the rest read it lightened, from أَنْجى. The two are of one meaning, because doubling and the hamza both make a verb transitive.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {تُؤْمِنُونَ}: it has no grammatical position, because it is an explanation of «تجارة». It is also possible that its position is nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "that commerce is: you believe", the khabar being the same as the mubtadaʾ so there is no need for a link (rābiṭ); or that its position is accusative through an implied verb, that is, "I mean: you believe". That is permissible on the assumption of «أَنْ», though it involves strain. The majority have «تُؤْمنون» as a khabar in form, with the nūn retained. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] has «آمِنوا» and «جاهِدوا» as two imperatives. Zayd ibn ʿAlī has «تؤمنوا» and «تجاهِدوا» with the nūn of the nominative dropped. As for the reading of the majority, the khabar is in the sense of an imperative, to which the two irregular readings point; for the reading of Zayd ibn ʿAlī rests on the omission of the lām of command, that is: «لِتؤمنوا ولتجاهِدوا», as in his saying:
4259 - محمدُ تَفْدِ نَفْسَك كلُّ نفسٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Muḥammad, let your soul be ransomed, every soul...)
and His saying {قُل لِّعِبَادِيَ الذين آمَنُواْ يُقِيمُواْ} [Ibrāhīm: 31] on one view, that is, «لِتَفْدِ» and «ليقيموا»; and for that reason the verb is jussive in its apodosis in His saying «يَغْفِرْ». Likewise their saying: «اتقى اللَّهَ امرؤ فَعَلَ خيراً يُثَبْ عليه», its implied form being: «ليتقِ اللهَ». Al-Akhfash said: "«تؤمنون» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of «تجارة»." This cannot be imagined except by the interpretation that the original was «أنْ تؤمنوا», and when «أن» was dropped the verb became nominative-ending (marfūʿ), as in his saying: 4260 - ألا أيُّهذا الزَّاجِريْ أَحْضُرُ الوغَى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O you who forbid me to attend the battle...) The original is «أن أَحْضُرَ». It is as if it were said: "Shall I direct you to a saving commerce: faith and striving?" This is a good meaning, were it not for the interpretation it involves. On this view it can be a badal from «تجارة». Al-Farrāʾ said: it is jussive as the answer to the question, which is His saying «هل أدلُّكم». The people differ on whether this statement is sound: some of them held it to be mistaken. Al-Zajjāj said: "It is not that when He directs them to what benefits them, He forgives them; He forgives them only if they believe and strive." He means that it is not consequent upon the mere question, nor upon the mere direction. Al-Mahdawī said: "It is sound only by construing it according to the meaning: that «يؤمنون» and «يُجاهدون» are an ʿaṭf bayān on His saying «هل أدلُّكم», as if the commerce were not known, what it is, and so it was clarified by faith and striving, it being the two of them in meaning; so it is as if it were said: 'Do you believe and strive?'" He said: "If you do not assume this implied form, it is not sound, because it becomes: 'if you are directed, He will forgive you,' whereas forgiveness becomes obligatory only by acceptance and faith, not by direction." Al-Zamakhsharī said something close to this as well. He also said: "«تُؤْمنون» is resumptive, as if they said: 'How shall we act?' and He said: 'You believe.'" Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«تُؤْمنون» is a verb with nominative ending, its implied form being: ذلك أنَّه تُؤْمنون," so he made it the khabar of «أَنَّ», and it and what is in its sphere are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. This is to be taken as an explanation of the meaning, not an explanation of the i'rāb, since there is no need for it.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {يَغْفِرْ}: there are several possibilities. The first is that it is jussive as the apodosis of a khabar in the sense of a command, as was set out earlier. The second is that it is jussive as the answer to the question, as al-Farrāʾ said, and its interpretation was given earlier. The third is that it is jussive by an implied condition, that is: "if you believe, He will forgive you."

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {وأخرى}: there are five possibilities regarding it. The first is that it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with its khabar implied, that is, "and for you", or "there", or "with Him is another quality (khaṣla)", or "another reward". And «تُحبُّونها» is a naʿt (adjective) of it. The second is that the khabar is a clause whose mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being: "it is victory", the clause being the khabar of «أُخْرى»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and it is very far-fetched, because it is an implied form for which there is no need. The third is that it is accusative through an omitted verb indicated by the context, that is, "and He will give you" or "He will grant you another reward". And «تُحبونها» is a naʿt of it also.
The fourth is that it is accusative through an implied verb explained by «تُحبُّونها», so that it is a case of ishtighāl (preoccupation), and then «تُحِبُّونها» is not a naʿt, because it explains the governor before it. The fifth is that it is genitive by ʿaṭf on «تجارة». This was weakened on the ground that it is not among what the commerce pointed to; it is only a reward from Allah. This view is reported from al-Akhfash.
His saying: {نَصْرٌ مِّن الله}: the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "that blessing, or the other bond (khalla), is victory." And «من الله» is a naʿt of it, or attached to it, that is, its beginning is from Him. The nominative ending of «نصرٌ» and «فتحٌ» is the reading of the majority; Ibn Abī ʿAbla put the three in the accusative. There are several possibilities in that, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī. The first is that they are accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ (specification). The second is that they are accusative as maṣdars, that is: they are given victory, and a near conquest is opened for them. The third is that they are accusative as a badal from «أُخْرى», while «أُخْرى» is accusative by an implied verb, as before, that is: "He will forgive you, admit you to gardens, and give you another," and then he substituted for it «نَصْراً وفَتْحاً قريباً».

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {أَنصَارَ الله}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «أنصاراً» with tanwīn and «لله» as a preposition and its genitive noun. The rest read «أنصارَ» without tanwīn, in iḍāfa to the noble Name. The orthography allows both readings. The lām may be added (mazīda) to the object for reinforcement, since the governor is derivative [of a verb], the original being: أنصاراً اللَّهَ; or it may be not added, the preposition and its genitive noun being a naʿt of «أَنْصاراً»; the first is clearer. As for the reading with iḍāfa, it derives from the aforementioned original. What supports the reading with iḍāfa is the consensus on it in His saying {نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ الله}. A disagreement here cannot be conceived because it is written with an alif.
His saying: {كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى}: there are several possibilities. The first is that the kāf is in the position of accusative with an implied "saying", that is: "We said that to them, as ʿĪsā said." The second is that it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "Be a being", as Makkī said, and there is room for objection, since they are not commanded to be a being. The third is that it is speech understood by its meaning rather than its wording, and al-Zamakhsharī inclined to it, for he said: "If you ask, what is the validity of the comparison, when its apparent sense is a comparison of their being helpers with the saying of ʿĪsā, blessings of Allah upon him, «مَنْ أنصاري»? I say: the comparison is understood by the meaning, and on that it is sound; the intended sense is: 'Be helpers of Allah as the disciples were helpers of ʿĪsā, when he said to them: {مَنْ أنصاري إِلَى الله}.'
The transitivity of «أَنْصَاري» with «إلى» was given in Āl ʿImrān, along with the differences of the people about it. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you ask: what is the meaning of His saying {مَنْ أنصاري إِلَى الله}? I say: its meaning must correspond to the disciples' reply: «نحن أنصارُ الله». What corresponds to it is that the meaning be: 'Who is a soldier of mine, turning toward the support of Allah?' The iḍāfa of «أَنْصاري» is different from the iḍāfa of «أنصار الله»; for the meaning of «نحن أنصارُ الله» is: 'We are those who help Allah', and the meaning of «مَنْ أنصاري» is: 'Who are the helpers who are devoted to me and will be with me in the support of Allah?' It is not sound for its meaning to be 'who will help me together with Allah', because that does not correspond to the reply. The proof of this is the reading of those who read «أنصارَ الله»." End. I say: he means that some claim that «إلى» is in the sense of «مع», that is, "Who are my helpers with Allah?" And his saying "the reading of those who read «أنصارَ الله»" means: if it were in the sense of «مع», its omission would not be sound in this reading. This is not necessarily so, because every reading has a meaning of its own, though it is preferable that the two readings agree.
His saying: {فَأَيَّدْنَا الذين آمَنُواْ على عَدُوِّهِمْ}: it is a case of putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun in both, to draw attention to the disbeliever's enmity toward the believer; for the original is: «فأيَّدْناهم عليهم», that is, "We supported the believers against the disbelievers of the two groups mentioned."

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ. . . (١١))
His saying (تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ): it is an explanation of (تِجَارَةٍ), so it may be in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute), or in the position of the nominative on the implied form "it is" (هِيَ); and أَنْ is omitted, and when it was omitted its governing effect ceased.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ. . . (١٢))
His saying (يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ): there are two views on why it is jussive. The first: it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an omitted condition indicated by the context, its implied form being "if you believe, He will forgive you", «تُؤْمِنُونَ» being in the sense of "believe!" (آمِنُوا). The second: it is the answer to what the interrogative indicates, and the meaning is: "will you accept, if I direct you?"
Al-Farrāʾ said: it is the answer to the interrogative according to the wording; this is far-fetched, because His directing them does not necessitate forgiveness for them.
«[Translator's note: the source has آمَنُوا (past), but the sense requires the imperative آمِنُوا; the imperative is followed here.]»

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأُخْرَى تُحِبُّونَهَا نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ. . . (١٣))
His saying (وَأُخْرَى): there are three views on its position. The first: accusative, on the implied form "and He will give you another". The second: it is accusative by a تُحِبُّونَ indicated by «تُحِبُّونَهَا». The third: its position is nominative, i.e. "and there is another", or the khabar (predicate) is «نَصْرٌ», i.e. "it is a victory".

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا أَنْصَارَ اللَّهِ كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ لِلْحَوَارِيِّينَ مَنْ أَنْصَارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنْصَارُ اللَّهِ فَآمَنَتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَكَفَرَتْ طَائِفَةٌ فَأَيَّدْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلَى عَدُوِّهِمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا ظَاهِرِينَ (١٤))
His saying (كَمَا قَالَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "I say to you as [ʿĪsā] said".
It is also said: it is construed according to the meaning, since the meaning is "help Allah as the disciples helped ʿĪsā son of Maryam, peace be upon him". And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ تَقُولُوا مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ (٢))
His saying {أَنْ تَقُولُوا}: it may be the fāʿil (agent) of {كَبُرَ}; or it may be on the implied form "it is" (هُوَ), the implied meaning being "that is grievous", and it would then be a badal (substitute). And {مَقْتًا} is a tamyīz (specification).
«[Translator's note: the source numbers this verse (٢); it is verse 3.]»

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيَانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ (٤))
And (صَفًّا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise (كَأَنَّهُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَمُبَشِّرًا بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالُوا هَذَا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ (٦))
His saying (مُصَدِّقًا): a corroborative ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida, circumstantial), and what governs it is رَسُولٌ, or what the context indicates.
And (مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «بَيْنَ».
And (مُبَشِّرًا) is also a ḥāl. And (اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ) is a clause in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of رَسُولٍ, or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَأْتِي».

ukberi-tibyan:8-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِئُوا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ (٨) هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ (٩))
His saying (مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ): with tanwīn [مُتِمٌّ نُورَهُ] and with annexation; its i'rab is evident.
And (بِالْهُدَى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رَسُولِهِ» ﷺ.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ṣaff (The Ranks)
Makkan
﷽
﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ وهو العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾ — we have already explained what is in His saying: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ﴾.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَ تَقُولُونَ ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ — the original is ”لِما“; the alif was elided because "mā" and the lām are like a single thing, and the use of ”ما“ with the lām in questions became frequent. If you pause on it you say ”لِمَهْ“, but one does not pause on it that way in the Quran, lest the muṣḥaf be contradicted; the reciter ought to join it (to what follows). This was said to them because they had said: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, we would do them, even if it meant losing our lives and our wealth." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿هَلْ أدُلُّكم عَلى تِجارَةٍ تُنْجِيكم مِن عَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 10] up to His saying: ﴿وَتُجاهِدُونَ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأمْوالِكم وأنْفُسِكم ذَلِكم خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 11]. Then, when the day of ”أُحُدٍ“ (Uḥud) came, those who turned away from the Prophet ﷺ turned away, until his front tooth was broken and he was wounded in his face; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَ تَقُولُونَ ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أنْ تَقُولُوا ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 3]. ”أنْ تَقُولُوا“ is in the position of the nominative, and ”مَقْتًا“ is accusative as a tamyīz (specification). The meaning is: "Your saying what you do not do is grievous as an object of loathing in the sight of Allah." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known what He loves, and said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَ في سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا كَأنَّهم بُنْيانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 4], i.e. a structure whose parts cleave to one another, no part of it leaving another. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He loves whoever stands firm in jihad in His way and keeps to his place like the chambers of a compact building. It is also possible — and Allah knows best — that He meant that their intentions be equal in fighting their enemy, so that in unity of purpose and mutual alliance they are like a compact structure.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ يا قَوْمِ لِمَ تُؤْذُونَنِي وقَدْ تَعْلَمُونَ أنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إلَيْكُمْ﴾ — we have explained in Sūrat ”اَلْأحْزابِ“ (al-Aḥzāb) the ways in which they had harmed him. ﴿فَلَمّا زاغُوا أزاغَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ means: they deviated from the truth and turned away from it, so Allah led them astray and turned their hearts aside.

His saying: ﴿واللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي القَوْمَ الفاسِقِينَ﴾ means: He does not guide one whom it is already in His knowledge that he is a transgressor.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾ — the position of ”إذْ قالَ عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ“ and of ”إذْ قالَ مُوسى“ alike is accusative. The meaning is: "Remember when Mūsā said, and remember when ʿĪsā son of Maryam said," i.e. recall to your people and your community the story of Mūsā and ʿĪsā, and what the end was of those who believed in them, and the end of those who disbelieved and harmed the prophets.

His saying: ﴿لِلْحَوارِيِّينَ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 14] — it is said that the disciples (al-ḥawāriyyūn) were so called because of the whiteness of their clothes; and it is said that they were fullers. ”اَلْحَوارِيُّونَ“ are the sincere intimates of the prophets and their elect, and the evidence for that is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «"Al-Zubayr is my paternal aunt's son and my disciple (ḥawāriyy) from my community,"» and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are disciples. The interpretation of ”اَلْحَوارِيُّونَ“ in the language is: those who have been purified and cleansed of every defect. Likewise ”اَلدَّقِيقُ الحُوّارى“ (fine white flour) comes from this; it was only so called because it is sifted from the kernel of the wheat and its pure part. Its interpretation with regard to people is that he is the one who, when his selection is reviewed time after time, is found free of defects. The root of ”اَلتَّحْوِيرُ“ in the language is from ”حارَ، يَحُورُ“, which is returning and repeating. This is its interpretation — and Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿مَن أنْصارِي إلى اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 14] means: "Who are my helpers together with Allah?" And some said: "Who are my helpers towards the help of Allah?" The poet said:
؎وَلَوْحُ ذِراعَيْنِ في بِرْكَةٍ ∗∗∗ إلى جُؤْجُؤٍ رَهِلِ المَنكِبِ
(And the broad flat of two forelegs in a chest, together with a breastbone, slack of shoulder.)
The meaning is ”اَلْكاهِلُ مَعَ جُؤْجُؤِ رَهَلِ المَنكِبِ“ (the withers together with a breastbone slack of shoulder). [Translator's note: the gloss uses الكاهل, a word not found in the verse as quoted; it is translated as written.]

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكم ذُنُوبَكم ويُدْخِلْكم جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ ومَساكِنَ طَيِّبَةً في جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ — this is the jawāb (apodosis) of ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ وتُجاهِدُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 11], because its meaning is the meaning of a command. The meaning is: "Believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives; He will forgive you your sins," i.e. if you do that He will forgive you. The evidence for that is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ”آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ“. Some grammarians erred and said: this is the answer to ”هَلْ“. This is a clear error: it is not the case that when the Prophet guides them to what benefits them Allah forgives them; Allah forgives them only when they believe and strive. So it is the answer to "تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ، وتُجاهِدُونَ، يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ". As for the jussive (majzūm) answer to a question, it is like your saying ”هَلْ جِئْتَنِي بِشَيْءٍ أُعْطِكَ مِثْلَهُ“ (have you brought me something, so that I may give you the like of it), the meaning being: "had you brought me (something) I would have given you," and "if you bring me (something) I will give you"; and likewise ”أيْنَ بَيْتُكَ أزُرْكَ“ (where is your house, that I may visit you).

His saying: ﴿فِي جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ means: in gardens of residence and permanence. One says ”عَدَنَ بِالمَكانِ“ when one has settled in a place.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأُخْرى تُحِبُّونَها نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ﴾ — the meaning is: "And you have another transaction which you love, and it is help from Allah and a near victory." If you wish, it is nominative as a badal (substitute) for ”أُخْرى“; the meaning is: "He will admit you to gardens, and you will have help from Allah and a near victory."

His saying: ﴿إنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إلَيْكم مُصَدِّقًا لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 6] — ”مُصَدِّقًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "I am the Messenger of Allah to you, in a state of confirming the Torah which preceded me, and in a state of giving glad tidings of a messenger" ﴿يَأْتِي مِن بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أحْمَدُ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 6]. It was read with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, ”مِن بَعْدِيَ“, and with the yāʾ quiescent and dropped from pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; but in writing it is retained: ”مِن بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أحْمَدُ“. The preferred choice according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl is to vowel this yāʾ with a fatḥa.

As for whoever read ”يَغْفِر لَّكُمْ“, assimilating the rāʾ into the lām, that is not permissible in recitation according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, because according to the two of them the rāʾ is not assimilated into the lām. Yet it has been transmitted from an imam of great standing in recitation, namely Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, and I do not reckon that he recited it except having heard it from the Arabs. Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the Basrans — except Abū ʿAmr — held that the lām is assimilated into the rāʾ, and that the rāʾ is not assimilated into the lām. The argument of those who said that the rāʾ is not assimilated into the lām is that the rāʾ is a strong, trilled letter, and if the rāʾ is assimilated into the lām its trill is lost. Their proof that it has an advantage over other letters in firmness is that you do not apply imāla (inclination of the vowel towards i) to a word of the pattern ”فاعِلٌ“ when at its beginning there is one of the velarized (iṭbāq) or elevated (mustaʿliya) letters. These are seven letters: four of them velarized, namely ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ and ẓāʾ, and three elevated, namely khāʾ, ghayn and qāf. You do not say ”هَذا صالِحٌ“ inclining the ṣād towards kasra; but if in the position of the lām there is a rāʾ, the kasra (imāla) is allowed: you say ”هَذا صارِمٌ“. And you do not say ”مَرَرْتُ بِضابِطٍ“ with imāla of the ḍād, but you do say ”مَرَرْتُ بِضارِبٍ“, for the rāʾ with kasra lowers the vowel of the velarized ṣād and ḍād. This chapter — the chapter of imāla — is one in grammar that the Basrans alone treated; the Kufans and the Medinans have nothing on it.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا أنْصارَ اللَّهِ﴾ — most of the reading is ”كُونُوا أنْصارَ اللَّهِ“, and it is the preferred choice because of their saying ”نَحْنُ أنْصارُ اللَّهِ“; because the two verses are in answer to ”كُونُوا أنْصارًا لِلَّهِ“: ”نَحْنُ أنْصارُ اللَّهِ“. And it is possible for ”نَحْنُ أنْصارُ اللَّهِ“ to be an answer to that. [Translator's note: the reasoning is compressed in the text as transmitted; the point is that the reading أنصارَ الله matches the disciples' reply نحن أنصارُ الله, while the variant أنصارًا لله can also be answered by it.] And ﴿واللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 8] was also read ”واللَّهُ مُتِمٌّ نُورَهُ“; both are good.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَأيَّدْنا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلى عَدُوِّهِمْ﴾ — the meaning of ”أيَّدْنا“ is: We strengthened; its derivation is from ”اَلْأيْدُ“, and ”اَلْأيْدُ“ is strength.
